title: User interface icons

location.series: City of Helsinki live visual identity guidelines

slide_intent: Give an interface icon a clear meaning and context because a familiar-looking symbol can still be ambiguous.
strategic_value: Consistent icon/text relationships can help Helsinki digital services remain understandable and accessible.
demonstration: This expanded webpage section lists eight HDS icon categories, explains label recommendations and exceptions, and shows icons in a digital-service context.
practical_value: Use a matching text label unless the icon is generally understood or its context makes its meaning clear.

content_islands.name: Interface specimens
content_islands.spec: Begin with eight large black icons, then group the broader icon family into eight numbered rows below the category list.

content_islands.name: Library categories
content_islands.spec: List eight functional groups and link to HDS definitions.

content_islands.name: Meaning and labels
content_islands.spec: Explain clear purpose, label recommendation and qualified exceptions.

content_islands.name: Contextual use
content_islands.spec: Show the digital-service example with its caption.

ingredient.name: Interface icon with label
ingredient.role: Make a digital action or content meaning identifiable.
ingredient.application: Use HDS icons with a matching label; omit labels only for generally known or contextually clear meanings.
ingredient.scope: Applies to digital-service icons; the section also permits their use as illustration icons but discourages purely decorative UI use.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explicitly explains that text labels clarify ambiguous icons and contradictory meanings harm usability/accessibility.
reference_purposes.Application: It provides label guidance and the familiar video-volume example.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Icons should have a clear purpose and must agree in meaning with their associated text/content.
